title: A spoken warning keeps hands off a hot stove around age three
summary: By about 3 years, most children avoid touching hot objects, such as a stove, when someone warns them, the U.S. CDC says.
body: Avoiding touching hot objects, like a stove, when you warn her, is a cognitive milestone on the CDC page for 3 years. Milestones on that page are skills most children, 75 percent or more, can do by the stated age. The page says Learn the Signs. Act Early. materials are not a substitute for standardized, validated developmental screening tools. The line is about understanding a warning. It does not describe a burn, a treatment, or any emergency telephone number. Drawing a circle when shown how is the other cognitive item and is not this claim. Another country's list can differ, and this is not a verdict on one child.
